subject: Re: NeuroPulse MAP — unit economics deep-dive and eval plan
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neuropulse.health>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Dr. Michael Carter <m.carter@neuropulse.health>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: MAP request — unit econ details and evaluation plan

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — Dr. Carter and I reviewed Redwood’s latency/cost slides and we want to fold a concrete unit-econ section into the mutual action plan (MAP) for our pilot. Procurement asked for a short packet showing: tokens/$ assumptions, how caching will reduce costs for repeated prompts, typical batching tradeoffs (latency vs throughput), and an expected estimate for the evaluation period (6-week pilot).

Can you:
- Share the MAP template you use for pilots
- Provide a starting tokens-per-dollar estimate for your recommended model(s) with and without caching
- Call out assumptions (avg prompt length, avg response length, cache hit rates, batch sizes) so we can validate against our traffic

I attached our traffic profile snapshot (neuropulse_traffic_profile.csv) — it’s sampled from a subset of our triage flows. We’re aiming to start the eval the week of Nov 8 and need cost guidance to get budget approval.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product Operations
NeuroPulse Health

Attachment: neuropulse_traffic_profile.csv (csv)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@neuropulse.health>
Cc: Dr. Michael Carter <m.carter@neuropulse.health>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP request — unit econ details and evaluation plan

Hi Lena — great to hear you’re ready to move this into a MAP. I’m attaching our MAP template and an initial token-model CSV that we’ll use to produce a pilot estimate. High-level starter assumptions below — these are conservative and meant to be validated against your traffic file:

Attachments: neuropulse_map_template.xlsx; neuropulse_token_model_v1.csv; redwood_map_notes.pdf

Quick assumptions we used for the draft estimate:
- Avg prompt tokens: 110 (pre-fill + user message)
- Avg completion tokens: 420 (average length for triage summaries)
- Tokens per API call: ~530
- Baseline tokens-per-dollar (hosted, non-quantized model): ~1,200 tokens/$ (this is our reference for Llama-2-like open model; your numbers will vary by model family and quantization)
- With standard 8-bit quantization and batching optimizations we typically see ~1.8–2.5x tokens/$ improvements on dedicated configurations

Caching and batching notes (to include in MAP):
- Prefix/KV caching: hitting on repeated system prompts or canned context reduces token spend on the prompt side. Based on similar customers, expect 10–25% token reduction if user flows reuse system/context phrases.
- Response caching (exact-match dedupe): small effect for triage summaries but helpful for templated replies (1–5% savings).
- Effective cache TTL assumption for planning: 10–20 minutes for session-level reuse; we’ll validate against your profile.
- Batching: we assume an average batch size of 6–10 for peak periods — increases throughput and tokens/$ materially but adds ~30–120ms tail latency depending on size and model. We can set latency SLOs in the MAP and configure burst vs steady-state batching policies.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll import your traffic sample into our modeler and push a draft MAP cost section by EOD Monday (Oct 20).
2) Marcus (cc’d) and I will run a small token-sensitivity sweep to show low/medium/high traffic scenarios.
3) We’ll propose a 6-week eval plan with a canary (week 1) + 5-week steady evaluation and an order-of-magnitude pilot price for procurement.

Do you have any hard constraints on average latency for triage completions? That will determine the batching trade-offs we present.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: neuropulse_map_template.xlsx (xlsx); neuropulse_token_model_v1.csv (csv); redwood_map_notes.pdf (pdf)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T20:10:00Z
Subject: FW: MAP request — unit econ details and evaluation plan

Jasmine — forwarding Lena’s traffic + your assumptions. Quick tech notes for the estimate:

- Traffic profile looks bursty (matches what they said). If peak 95th pctl batching is enabled, we can safely target batch=8 median, batch=16 peak for dedicated pool. That would increase tokens/$ by ~2x vs no-batching baseline in our tests.
- Cache effectiveness: their sample shows ~12% repeated prefixes (session templates) — I’d budget 12–15% prompt-side token reduction out of the gate.
- We should prepare two model options in the MAP: hosted standard (faster onboarding, higher per-token cost) and dedicated quantized (lower tokens/$, needs ~4–6 GPU reserved for pilot).
- Recommend we include a sensitivity table: tokens/$ at cache hit rates 0%, 12%, 25% and batch sizes [1,6,12].

Neha — can you run the sensitivity sweep (low/med/high traffic) and paste the delta table? I’ll draft the deployment + cost rows for the MAP.

—Marcus

On Oct 18, 2026, at 18:05, jasmine_liu@redwood.com wrote:
> [quoted above]

Cc: Dr. Michael Carter <m.carter@neuropulse.health>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:33:00Z

Thanks Jasmine — that looks aligned with what procurement wanted. Two follow-ups from our side:

1) We prefer batching where steady-state latency stays under 600ms for triage completions. If batching pushes above that in median, we’ll need to prioritize lower-latency config even if tokens/$ are lower.
2) Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a pilot price/credit for the 6-week eval — ideally a blended token rate or a capped spend for pilot. If you can add a recommended pilot credit and a short paragraph describing how it maps to tokens (e.g., X tokens ~= $Y) that would help our CFO sign-off.

We attached a PO draft to show required procurement fields (NeuroPulse_PO_draft.pdf). We’re targeting kickoff week of Nov 8 as noted — would you be able to deliver the MAP cost rows and sensitivity table before Oct 22?

Appreciate it — Lena

Attachment: NeuroPulse_PO_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Action: approve pilot credit and finalize MAP cost rows (NeuroPulse)

Team — Lena confirmed latency constraint (median <600ms) and asked for a recommended pilot price / credit mapping to tokens for procurement. I drafted two pilot options in the attached MAP notes:

- Option A (hosted, fast onboarding): 400k tokens credit (~$320 at our list rates) — covers the 1-week canary + light steady eval; expected spend if no caching: ~350k tokens for 6 weeks baseline scenario.
- Option B (dedicated, quantized reservation): 1.6M tokens equivalent (~$900 blended) — assumes batch-driven throughput improvements and 15% cache hit; this buys more runway and keeps median latency ~450ms with batch policies.

We need sign-off on Option B discounting and on the dedicated-reservation sizing. Marcus, I believe the dedicated VM sizing you suggested (4 GPUs reserved) is correct for their traffic shape. Neha — please paste the sensitivity table we ran and confirm the token deltas used for Option B. Rishi — can you approve the pilot credit/discount structure or advise on negotiated cap?

If we can lock this by EOD Monday (Oct 25) we’ll deliver the MAP cost appendix and Sensitivity workbook to Lena and Procurement and be on track for the Nov 8 kickoff.

Thanks — Jasmine

Attachment: redwood_map_notes.pdf (pdf)
